.SHORT TERM /THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Issued at 329 AM CDT Thu Sep 10 2026

Upper-level quasi-zonal flow ahead of a trough over the Central 
Plains will continue to support waves of showers and thunderstorms 
through at least the morning as a series of mid-level vort 
maxes/MCVs track eastward. Most of these showers and thunderstorms 
are expected to be focused around the I-70 and I-44 corridors where 
low-level FGEN is forecast to ebb and flow with multiple narrow LLJ 
cores translating eastward. With decreasing (increasing) surface-
based instability (convective inhibition), the already low threat of 
severe weather has further decreased, but locally heavy rainfall 
still warrants monitoring through the morning. With anomalous PW 
exceeding 2", deep-warm cloud depths, and around 1000 J/kg of 
MUCAPE; ingredients are in place for efficient, high rainfall rates. 
In fact, rates of 1.5 to 2.5"/hr were estimated with the strongest 
thunderstorms earlier this evening. The 00z HREF LPMM of QPF valid 
after 08z (3 am) this morning, indicates 1 to locally 3" of 
additional rainfall near the I-70 and I-44 corridors. Soils are 
still dry, but there is a swath of 1 to 3" of rainfall from last 
evening that extends from near Washington, MO to Belleville, IL that 
has elevated streamflows and could precondition soils for isolated 
flash flooding if additional heavy rainfall overlaps that area. 
Otherwise, the threat of flash flooding is still low with most, if 
not all, of this rainfall being just beneficial.

It is not completely clear how quickly precipitation will end late 
this morning through afternoon with the CWA still remaining just 
ahead of the upper-level trough axis and in an equatorward jet 
entrance region, but there should at least be a decrease in 
thunderstorms and overall coverage of showers as the effective cold 
front progresses further south of the CWA. That being said, there is 
a weak, secondary cold front that advances southeastward into the 
evening CWA that 15 to 30 percent of HREF membership has resulting 
in additional isolated to scattered showers, perhaps a rumble of 
thunder. With widespread clouds and precipitation lingering well 
into the day, high temperatures will fail to warm above 80 F in many 
areas.
